entities.name: Rinnal
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Rinnal, a figure of profound significance within Irish mythology, is recorded as a High King of Ireland belonging to the Fir Bolg, a legendary people believed to have inhabited Ireland before the arrival of the Tuatha Dé Danann. His ascent to power is a pivotal moment in the mythical cycles, marking a shift in the Fir Bolg dynasty and, more importantly, establishing a technological precedent. Though specific dates are absent from the mythical chronology, his reign is typically situated in the distant prehistory of Ireland, making him a foundational character in the island's legendary past and an early symbol of martial innovation.

His path to the high kingship involved the overthrow of Fiacha Cennfinnán, his predecessor, an event emblematic of the often-violent transitions of power described in early Irish narratives. Rinnal's most enduring legacy, however, is the assertion that he was the first king in Ireland to utilize spearheads in warfare. This detail, while mythical, suggests a conceptual leap in military technology, moving beyond simpler bludgeons or sharpened sticks to more sophisticated, metal-tipped weapons, thereby enhancing the effectiveness and lethality of the Fir Bolg armies during his purported reign.

The introduction of spearheads, whether a literal historical event or a symbolic representation of technological progress, fundamentally altered the mythological landscape of Irish combat, influencing subsequent accounts of battles and heroic deeds. Rinnal's reign, typically ascribed a duration of five years in the Lebor Gabála Érenn (The Book of Invasions), cemented his place in the legendary succession of Irish kings, contributing to the rich tapestry of pre-Christian Irish political and military history. His story thus serves as an early narrative of innovation and dynastic change.

His story is crucial for understanding the chronological and technological evolution within Irish legendary history.
